carousels.name: Most people saw p*rn before they were 13

slides.title: Over half of teens have seen p*rn [[by age 13.]]
slides.sub: Your p*rn addiction may have started before you could understand it.

slides.title: It started [[early]]
slides.body: In a 2023 Common Sense Media survey of U.S. teens, 54% had seen p*rn by 13 — and 15% at 10 or younger.

slides.title: Earlier exposure, [[higher]] risk
slides.body: A University of Glasgow review found earlier first exposure to p*rn was linked to more frequent use and a higher risk of compulsive use. It's a pattern, not proof — but it's worth knowing.

slides.title: Not your [[fault]]. Still your move.
slides.body: You didn't pick the age p*rn found you. But you can pick what you do about it now.

slides.title: What to do [[with this]]
items: Drop the self-hate — p*rn found you young.
Take responsibility for today, not for age 12.
Protect younger people in your life from early p*rn.
Start your recovery — it's never too late.

carousels.name: The 'I'm not enough' belief behind p*rn addiction

slides.title: Under your p*rn addiction is one belief: [["I'm not enough."]]
slides.sub: And p*rn keeps proving it to you.

slides.title: The [[shame]] cycle
slides.body: Each round of p*rn makes the belief feel more true.

slides.title: P*rn [[numbs]] the belief
slides.body: When you feel unworthy, p*rn gives a few minutes of not feeling anything. Then the shame arrives — and the belief gets louder.

slides.title: Challenge the [[belief]]
slides.body: Write it down: "I'm not enough." Then list three things that prove it wrong. You are more than your p*rn addiction.

slides.title: Build [[enough]]
items: Notice wins — even one p*rn-free evening counts.
Talk to someone who sees the real you.
Get help if the belief is heavy — a therapist can go deep.
slides.note: What would you tell someone who feels "not enough"? 👇

slides.title:
You are enough.
[[You don't need p*rn.]]

carousels.name: Quitting p*rn vs recovering from p*rn addiction

slides.title: Quitting p*rn isn't the same as [[recovering from p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: White-knuckling gets you days. Recovery gets you free.

slides.title: White-[[knuckling]]
slides.body: Gritting your teeth, counting days, hoping the urge doesn't win tonight. It can work for a while — but the reasons you used p*rn are still there.

slides.title: Real [[recovery]]
slides.body: Understanding why you turned to p*rn — stress, loneliness, boredom, shame — and building a life that meets those needs. That's what lasts.

slides.title: You need [[both]]
slides.body: Blocking p*rn buys you time. Recovery uses that time well. Stop the behavior AND heal the reason.

slides.title: Signs of [[real]] recovery
items: You know what drives your p*rn urges.
Your life feels better, not just p*rn-free.

carousels.name: What to say to yourself in the first minute of a p*rn urge

slides.title: What to say to yourself [[the moment a p*rn urge hits.]]
slides.sub: The first minute decides the night.

slides.title: "This is an [[urge]], not an order."
slides.body: A p*rn urge feels like a command. It isn't. You can feel it and still say no.

slides.title: "It will [[pass]]."
slides.body: Urges rise and fall. Most fade within minutes if you don't feed them. You've outlasted p*rn urges before.

slides.title: "What do I [[actually]] need?"
slides.body: Tired? Lonely? Stressed? Bored? P*rn is rarely the real answer — name the real need.

slides.title: "Future me will [[thank]] me."
slides.body: Picture tomorrow morning — clear-headed, proud, no shame. That version of you is worth ten minutes of discomfort.

slides.title: Can't read a page without your mind drifting? [[P*rn might be part of it.]]
slides.sub: How endless clicking trains a restless brain.

slides.title: Trained to [[click]]
slides.body: Skipping, searching, opening the next tab — p*rn use is built on constant switching. Many people say that restlessness spills into everything.

slides.title: Boredom [[intolerance]]
slides.body: After years of instant p*rn on demand, a slow book or a long task can feel unbearable. That's a skill you can rebuild.

slides.title: Focus comes [[back]]
slides.body: Many people report sharper focus after cutting out p*rn and endless scrolling. Everyone's different — but it's worth testing for yourself.

slides.title: Rebuild your [[focus]]
items: Read 10 pages a day — no phone nearby.
Get bored on purpose — let your brain rest.
